relationship_strength_review.basis: Enforcement of approved authorisations directly governs the proposed information-access boundary.

Task-limited authorised access is a substantial, independently assessable restriction on information access. It supports the permission boundary within assigned tasks; it does not prove the entire occurrence test.

Protection of selected information and selected confidentiality and/or integrity properties at rest substantially supports the information/custody boundary at rest. Organisation-defined parameters are preserved; the relationship does not cover every lifecycle stage.

Protection of the selected confidentiality and/or integrity property during transmission substantially supports the information/custody boundary for that stage. This is partial lifecycle coverage, not weak evidentiary correspondence.
The explicit authenticator-content disclosure and modification protection directly supports the custody boundary without any downstream misuse condition.
Identity verification at initial distribution is a substantial recipient-custody control at that lifecycle stage. It does not prove protection during later handling.

Specific individual and device authenticator-protection controls substantially support custody protection. The implemented control and protected handling outcome still require independent occurrence evidence.
